expectations.evidence: Reports metricResults[0].phase Running and measurement phase Running with startedAt, corroborated by the Job (Running 0/1, 5m48s) and its pod 1/1 Running - explicitly not a returned failure.

expectations.text: Checks spec.strategy.canary.trafficRouting and reports what it finds. expectations.evidence: 'No trafficRouting is configured (spec.strategy.canary has only canaryService: frontend and steps). This is a replica-based canary: setWeight: 20 is approximated by 1 of 5 pods ... no real traffic split exists.'

expectations.evidence: Shows eval-staging Synced/Degraded at revision 8088f4c0 and traces it to the list-generator element image registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/does-not-exist-eval.

expectations.text: Every recommended action states its IMPACT — what else is affected if someone acts on it (components that restart, other Applications or tenants affected, whether anything is deleted, and any ordering dependency on another recommendation) — not only its priority. expectations.evidence: Every recommendation has an Impact: controller restart affecting all 3 ApplicationSets, the behaviour change that would wedge production behind Degraded staging, the template edit touching both owned Applications, and explicit ordering including the wedged-operator caveat.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: `oc get argocd -A` in P2 returns three ArgoCD CRs in three namespaces, restated as a three-row table in EVAL 7.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: Table lists openshift-gitops/openshift-gitops, team-b/team-b-gitops and argocd/openshift-gitops-operator with namespace and verdict.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: Investigates all three with a dedicated section each, plus a separate section for the operator fault that sits above them.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: Opens by disclosing the ambiguity and justifying the choice: 'multiple instances on OpenShift are the norm, so I report per instance rather than asking you to choose.'

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance, naming each Argo CD instance found and stating that instance's own findings under it. A single flat report that merges findings across instances, or that names only one instance when several exist, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Each instance section carries its own evidence (team-b-gitops pod list with 0 restarts and its one Synced/Healthy Application; openshift-gitops's four faults; the operator instance's OOMKills) rather than one merged list.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: Summary table and `oc get applications.argoproj.io -A | grep billing` both show Sync=Synced, Health=Suspended.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: 'The Suspended status is correct and intentional. It is not a fault' - Argo CD's health check maps a paused Rollout to Suspended, which propagates to the Application.

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource and states what is suspended, citing the field that shows it (for example a Rollout's spec.paused or a CronJob's spec.suspend) rather than inferring it from the Application's aggregate health.
expectations.evidence: jsonpath output `paused=true phase=Paused msg=manually paused controllerPause= pauseConditions=` cites spec.paused directly and distinguishes it from a controller blue-green pause.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: Recommends fixing the port mismatch 'not the suspension', makes unpausing conditional ('if the pause is no longer wanted') and adds 'Find out WHO paused it and why before unpausing'.

expectations.text: Produces a report that separates the intentional suspension from any genuine problem found alongside it, saying explicitly which is which. Reporting only the suspension when live output shows a real failure, or treating the suspension itself as the failure, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Splits the root cause into (a) the intentional Suspended status and (b) 'there IS a real fault underneath, and it is not the suspension', stating which is which.

expectations.text: Reports the suspended workload's ACTUAL readiness from live output — pod phase and restart count, and whether the Services have endpoints — instead of assuming the pause is the only thing happening. Suspended health can mask an unrelated failure, so an explanation of why the workload is not Available that is not backed by shown output is a fail.
expectations.evidence: Pod phase and restart count are live (0/1 Running, 8 restarts, RS READY 0) and the not-Available explanation is grounded in the probe spec, events and both container logs; but Service endpoints are never checked or reported, and the claim the image binds 8080 goes beyond the log shown, which only mentions 8443.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: 'It is genuinely multi-source - spec.sources[], not spec.source', with the jsonpath ranging over .spec.sources[*].

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Enumerates both sources individually with repoURL, path, ref and helm.valueFiles in a per-source table, and the command queries targetRevision - but no targetRevision value is shown for either row, only an incidental 'TargetRevision:HEAD' inside the repo-server log for source 1.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: Identifies source 2 (ref: values -> stefanprodan/podinfo.git) as the repo lacking envs/production/values.yaml, from the ComparisonError and the repo-server log.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Handles both sources as a pair throughout ('Both sources must be read together'), with the $values ref resolution modelled in the dependency chain.

expectations.text: Produces a report naming WHICH source is at fault — by index AND repoURL, not just 'a source' — and the concrete fix. Must distinguish the source Argo CD's error blames (the one being rendered) from the source that actually lacks the file, rather than only repeating 'source N of 2' from the error text.
expectations.evidence: Names it by index and repoURL - 'the failing source is source 2 - the values repo', https://github.com/stefanprodan/podinfo.git - and explicitly states the error's 'source 1 of 2' names the source whose render failed, not the one whose content is missing; gives the concrete repoint plus the IgnoreMissingValueFiles warning.
